neighborhood.name: Bernal Heights
neighborhood.summary: A neighborhood-scale guide to Bernal's hidden fog-fed texture: walls, bark, slopes, stairs, and wet edges where mosses, liverworts, and lichens become legible through place-based stories.
neighborhood.why_here: Bernal is a strong first chapter because it is walkable, visually varied, and rich in microhabitats that can turn an ordinary neighborhood walk into an atlas of urban texture.

walk.title: Post-Rain Bernal Loop
walk.terrain: hilly sidewalks, stairs, and park paths
walk.start_label: To be field-chosen in Bernal Heights Park area
walk.end_label: To be field-chosen near a Cortland-adjacent finish

stops.title: North Slope Wall Start
stops.location_hint: Lower north side of Bernal Heights Park
stops.short_summary: A candidate opening stop focused on the easiest-to-read urban moss texture near the base of the hill.
stops.why_here: This stop is meant to teach the atlas lens quickly: seams, shade, and retained moisture can make moss legible almost immediately in Bernal.
stops.seasonality: Best after rain; likely visible year-round in shaded conditions.
stops.species_notes: Candidate wall mosses and lichens; do not name taxa until field-verified.

stops.title: Stair Edge Moisture Band
stops.location_hint: Public stair corridor near the hill approach
stops.short_summary: A candidate stop for showing how runoff, seams, and shade create miniature growth lanes in everyday infrastructure.
stops.why_here: Stairs and retaining edges can make water movement visible, which turns this stop into a strong lesson about how moss worlds assemble in plain sight.
stops.seasonality: Strongest after rain or morning moisture; verify persistence across drier periods.
stops.species_notes: Candidate wall mosses and moisture-tolerant associates; exact taxa unknown.

stops.title: Street Tree Bark Strip
stops.short_summary: A candidate bark stop that expands the atlas from walls into the neighborhood's second texture layer on living trunks.
stops.why_here: Street trees can carry subtle but persistent moss and lichen patterns that make Bernal feel richer than its streetscape suggests at first glance.
stops.seasonality: Likely useful year-round; strongest after rain or on shaded bark.
stops.species_notes: Candidate bark mosses and lichens; possible Alsia, Homalothecium, Ramalina, or related groups.

stops.title: Garden Edge Liverwort Pocket
stops.short_summary: A candidate wet-edge stop where Bernal may briefly behave like a tiny urban wetland.
stops.why_here: This stop matters if it proves that small irrigation or seep patterns can produce liverwort-friendly habitat inside an otherwise dry urban neighborhood.
stops.seasonality: Most promising after rain or sustained irrigation; may disappear visually in drier periods.
stops.species_notes: Candidate liverworts such as Lunularia or Marchantia; field confirmation required.

stops.title: Retaining Wall Gradient
stops.location_hint: Sloped residential edge with visible aspect change
stops.short_summary: A candidate comparison stop showing how aspect and runoff can change the texture of the same block.
stops.why_here: This is one of the most useful atlas-style stories if it can show two moisture realities only a few steps apart.
stops.seasonality: Best after rain when the contrast between wet and dry faces is clearest.
stops.species_notes: Candidate wall mosses, lichens, and dry-tolerant associates; names deferred until fieldwork.

stops.title: Bernal Summit Exposure Stop
stops.location_hint: Park upper slope or exposed edge
stops.short_summary: A candidate high-exposure stop focused on lichen, wind, fog, and sun pressure rather than lush green abundance.
stops.why_here: This stop expands the product beyond a simple 'more moss is better' story by showing how exposed Bernal edges create a different texture language.
stops.seasonality: Potentially strong year-round; verify whether post-rain conditions improve readability.
stops.species_notes: Candidate lichens and hardy exposed-site taxa; Niebla, Xanthoria, or related groups are possible but unconfirmed.

stops.title: Rock and Crack Colony
stops.short_summary: A candidate stop for showing how tiny fractures and rough surfaces create habitat in the city.
stops.why_here: If strong enough, this stop helps explain how Bernal's built environment acts like a patchwork of microclimates rather than inert hardscape.
stops.seasonality: Most readable after rain; may still work year-round if the texture contrast is strong.
stops.species_notes: Candidate rock mosses, lichens, or mixed crust communities; precise identification deferred.

stops.title: Tree Base Shadow Ring
stops.location_hint: Mature tree base in public right-of-way or park
stops.short_summary: A candidate stop centered on the damp shadow ring that can form around tree bases and root flares.
stops.why_here: This stop matters if it helps walkers notice how drip lines, bark, and shade persistence create a small recurring habitat pattern around street trees.
stops.seasonality: Likely best after rain or in long-shaded conditions.
stops.species_notes: Candidate bark and root-flare mosses or lichens; field notes needed before making taxon claims.

stops.title: Fence Line Texture Shift
stops.location_hint: Edge condition between maintained and rough ground
stops.short_summary: A candidate edge-habitat stop about what maintenance preserves or erases small urban moss worlds.
stops.why_here: This stop can connect ecology to neighborhood care patterns by showing how trimming, sweeping, and disturbance affect what survives.
stops.seasonality: Needs field verification; may depend heavily on recent moisture and maintenance timing.
stops.species_notes: Candidate mixed moss and lichen assemblage; exact groups unknown.

stops.title: Neighborhood Finish Stop
stops.location_hint: Walk endpoint near everyday foot traffic
stops.short_summary: A candidate closing stop that returns the story to ordinary Bernal life and repeat noticing.
stops.why_here: The walk should end in a place that makes the atlas feel portable, so walkers leave seeing the neighborhood differently rather than finishing at a purely scenic endpoint.
stops.seasonality: Flexible; verify whether the site works both after rain and in drier conditions.
stops.species_notes: Mixed candidate moss, lichen, or texture-layer story; exact taxa secondary to the closing narrative.
